text: If you're not doing this, you're...
debunkingText: This is a Fear Mongering tactic. It bypasses logic by making you feel scared. A claim's validity isn't determined by how scary its alternative is.

text: Everyone is doing this new 7-day cleanse...
debunkingText: Your body has a built-in, highly effective "detox" system: your liver and kidneys. Most "cleanses" are just a form of fasting that don't "clean" anything.

text: I never thought this was possible... I lost 20lbs...
debunkingText: Before/after photos are easy to fake. A simple change in lighting, posture, angle, or just sucking in can create a dramatically misleading illusion.

text: The one trick that will change your life forever...
debunkingText: Be wary of any "one simple trick" or "cure-all." Health is complex, and real solutions are almost never a single, magical secret.

text: Why use harsh chemicals when you can use this...
debunkingText: This is the Appeal to Nature fallacy. "Natural" does not automatically mean "safe" or "better." Cyanide, arsenic, and snake venom are all 100% natural.

text: Big Pharma doesn't want you to know this...
debunkingText: This is a conspiracy tactic to create an "Us vs. Them" narrative. Claims of "suppressed cures" almost never have verifiable evidence to support them.

text: A prominent scientist says doing this every day...
debunkingText: This relies on Vague Authority. Who is this scientist? Where was this published? If no verifiable source is given, the claim is worthless. Real science is specific.

text: Rediscover the forgotten secrets of the ancients...
debunkingText: This is the Appeal to Tradition fallacy. The age of a practice has no bearing on its effectiveness. We've abandoned many "ancient" practices (like bloodletting) for very good reasons.

text: A recent study hinted that this could be effective...
debunkingText: This is Cherry Picking. It highlights one tiny piece of data (like a single table) while ignoring the full context, the study's conclusion, or all other research that contradicts it.

text: The numbers don't lie! Just look at this chart...
debunkingText: A graph can be easily manipulated to lie. Common tricks include truncating the Y-axis (not starting at zero) or cherry-picking data points to make a trend look more dramatic.

text: My cousin's best friend lost 60lbs with this...
debunkingText: An Anecdote ("it worked for my cousin") is not data. It's a single data point with no control group, and it completely ignores the powerful placebo effect.

text: Mainstream 'experts' say just 'eat in moderation'...
debunkingText: This is a Strawman attack. It misrepresents the opposing argument (e.g., "food pyramid") to make it look weak and easy to attack.

text: It's all about the secret biovibrational harmonization...
debunkingText: This uses Pseudoscientific Jargon to sound impressive. Terms like "biovibrational" or "quantum energy" are scientifically meaningless and are used to confuse, not clarify.

text: All your health problems stem from one single thing...
debunkingText: This is the Single-Cause Fallacy. Complex problems like disease are almost never caused by one single thing. This extreme oversimplification is a classic red flag.

text: My friend went gluten-free and her acne cleared up...
debunkingText: This confuses Correlation with Causation. Just because B happened after A doesn't mean A caused B. Maybe she also cut out sugar, or simply got older.

text: To get the full effect...you have to try my new...
debunkingText: This is a classic sales funnel. The "free" advice creates a problem, and the Financial Gain tactic conveniently sells you the one "true" solution.

text: All your friends are already doing this...
debunkingText: This is the Bandwagon Fallacy. The popularity of an idea has zero impact on its validity. "Everyone is doing it" is a social pressure tactic, not a scientific argument.

text: Your body is a temple. Don't pollute it...
debunkingText: This is an Appeal to Purity. This emotionally charged language is not scientific. Your body is not "dirty" or "polluted" in the way these products claim.

text: Leading experts and university studies agree...
debunkingText: This is an appeal to Vague Authority. Which "leading experts"? What "university studies"? If they don't provide a specific, verifiable source, the claim is empty.

text: They're trying to silence me. My last post was flagged...
debunkingText: This is a conspiracy tactic to build authority. Claiming to be "silenced" frames criticism as persecution, making the influencer look like a brave martyr speaking the truth.

text: I've compiled all my secrets into a new e-book...
debunkingText: This is a Bait-and-Switch. The "free" information on the social media post is just an advertisement designed to get you to pay for the "real" secrets.

text: I found this in a lost medical manuscript...
debunkingText: This is a Special Knowledge claim. It suggests the "truth" is hidden and only available to a select few. Real scientific knowledge is published openly for all to review and test.

text: Want one-on-one help? I'm opening 5 spots...
debunkingText: This uses Artificial Scarcity ("5 spots left!") to create urgency and drive impulse buys for expensive, often unaccredited, coaching services.

text: Your doctor will tell you to just 'eat less'...
debunkingText: This is an "Us vs. Them" conspiracy. It tries to create complete distrust in the entire medical profession to position the guru as the only one with the "real" answers.

text: That other 'guru' is a fraud. I have info that...
debunkingText: This is an Ad Hominem attack. It attacks the person ("fraud," "liar") instead of their argument or evidence. It's a deflection tactic to avoid a real debate.

text: These so-called 'scientists' are just paid puppets...
debunkingText: This is a broad Attack on the scientific method. Science is a process of being wrong and correcting itself; that's its strength. This tactic uses past corrections as "proof" the whole system is untrustworthy.

text: To the 'skeptic' in my comments... Blocked...
debunkingText: This is Creating an Echo Chamber. By blocking all criticism and labeling skeptics as "trolls," the influencer maintains a purely supportive community, making their claims seem more valid.
